The audit deliberately exempts requiredFiles from the role check. R2 residual: the git ls-files output is filtered with Test-Path, and non-existent entries are dropped silently. With default core.quotePath, a non-ASCII path is emitted C-quoted, fails Test-Path and is omitted. The audit uses the same enumeration and would not detect the omission. PowerShell's native-output decoding can also mangle UTF-8 names. Consider `git -c core.quotePath=false ls-files -z` with explicit UTF-8 decoding. Alternatively, fail when a listed path is missing instead of filtering it out, and report deleted-but-tracked files separately.

R2 residual: --others --exclude-standard also indexes untracked, non-ignored scratch files under implementations/csharp/tests. That is acceptable for a hashed draft. A WP09 snapshot will probably want tracked-only enumeration, or an explicit note on the untracked members.
